text:
carla: heads-up: deploy-bot refused to publish core-auth:pr-6123 to staging. error says attestation digest does not match final manifest.

deploy-bot: publish rejected: attestation_digest_mismatch.
  tag=staging-pr-6123
  client-computed=sha256:4b7f...
  attested-digest=sha256:aa77...
  action=abort

josh: wait — so cosign attestation is present but points at a different digest? how did that happen?

ci-bot: last pipeline run for PR-6123 produced artifact ci-build-6123 -> computed manifest sha256:4b7f... (2025-10-25T09:10:02Z). cosign signed artifact at pipeline end, but sign step shows timestamp 2025-10-25T09:11:10Z and digest recorded aa77... (mismatch).

anika: possibilities: (1) a repush/timestamp race after sign (2) signing step used a cached tag that pointed to older digest (3) mirror rewrite/manifest canonicalization changed ordering before attestation.

carla: we should pin the staging slot to last-known-good digest and not promote. do we have last-good?

deploy-bot: previous_staging_digest for core-auth -> sha256:98c3... (2025-10-24T23:02:05Z)

josh: plan: (A) hold promote for core-auth (B) republish the exact CI artifact without reassembling layers (no rebuild) to a new tag with explicit digest tag (buildid-6123) (C) re-run cosign sign/attestation against that exact manifest (D) verify across mirrors then canary.

release-manager: approve hold. remove from today's EU promote window and add to release notes: "core-auth staging publish blocked by attestation/digest mismatch; republish + re-attest in progress."

anika: quick commands I will run from CI host (reuse ci-build-6123):
```
# republish without rebuild
publishbot republish --artifact ci-build-6123 --target-tag staging-repub-6123 --force --preserve-manifest
# sign with KMS-backed key
cosign sign --kms kms://projects/redwood/keys/cosign-key core-auth:staging-repub-6123
# verify
cosign verify --key kms://projects/redwood/keys/cosign-key core-auth:staging-repub-6123
```

infra-bot: checking mirror and proxy logs for any rewrite rules. mirror-proxy-9 had no 5xx spikes but gcr-mirror job applied a transform in the past for legacy "org.redwood" label normalization (INF-2060). could that change manifest canonicalization? tagging/mutating registries can cause signed-manifest mismatches.

josh: good catch. if mirror or a registry layer altered annotations/labels during replication, the attestation digest wouldn't match. we need to ensure the attestation is created after any canonicalization and against the final, immutable digest we will serve.

carla: so republish + sign should attach attestation to the final manifest we plan to deploy. also add a guard in publishbot: refuse to accept an attestation that references a digest other than the finalized manifest.

anika: republish started. watch: https://publishbot.internal/ops/6123

ci-bot: republish finished: staging-repub-6123 -> sha256:4b7f...
cosign sign completed and attestation uploaded. cosign verify -> OK. provenance attached via provenance-checker.

deploy-bot: publish ok for staging tag staging-repub-6123 -> sha256:4b7f.... canary scheduled.

josh: starting canary now. monitoring pulls, cosign/attestation presence on mirrors, and error budgets.

infra-bot: I filed INF-2060 follow-up to audit mirror transform rules and add a preflight verification that mirrors do not mutate signatures/annotations.

release-manager: canary running — hold remains for prod promote until canary green and INF-2060 follow-up. release notes updated.

carla: quick retro items: (1) publishbot: enforce attestation-digest check fail-fast, (2) CI: ensure sign step runs after final push confirmation, (3) mirrors: add non-mutating guarantee or canonicalization whitelist.

josh: canary green after 18m. ready for manual promote outside EU change window tomorrow morning.

release-manager: thanks all. leaving hold in changelog until promote completes. will add INF-2060 postmortem link when available. :thumbsup:
